title: Rob Lowe Explains Why The Floor Films in Ireland Instead of Los Angeles
excerpt:
Flying roughly 100 American contestants abroad can be more economical than filming in LA.
The comparison highlights changing television production costs.
body_md:
Rob Lowe, host of Fox's competition series The Floor, has highlighted the surprising economics behind filming the American game show in Ireland rather than Los Angeles. Even transporting roughly one hundred contestants across the Atlantic can make financial sense for the production.

The example illustrates how television companies increasingly weigh total production expenses rather than simply choosing a studio near their network headquarters.

CinemaBlend identifies several possible contributing factors, including labor requirements, contestant accommodation costs and Ireland's production tax incentives. These are elements of the outlet's analysis and should not all be treated as direct quotes from Lowe.

While shows such as The Pitt and Abbott Elementary continue filming in Los Angeles, other productions have shifted locations. Shark Tank and American Idol have moved production activity to Atlanta, while The Masked Singer has relocated to New Jersey.

California has introduced incentives intended to retain more film and television work, but the broader cost debate continues. The Floor provides a concrete example of how financial considerations can outweigh the logistical complexity of international travel.
